desc:
You are given a rectangular grid of integers matrix and a list of queries. Each query is [r1, c1, r2, c2] and asks for the sum of all cells matrix[i][j] with r1 ≤ i ≤ r2 and c1 ≤ j ≤ c2 (rows and columns are 0-indexed, both ends inclusive).

Return an array with the answer to every query, in the same order as the queries.

matrix = [[3, 0, 1, 4],
          [5, 6, 3, 2],
          [1, 2, 0, 1]]
queries = [[0, 0, 1, 1], [1, 1, 2, 3], [0, 1, 2, 1]]
result = [14, 14, 8]
constraints: 0 ≤ r1 ≤ r2 < rows and 0 ≤ c1 ≤ c2 < columns
hints: Adding up every cell of a rectangle for every query costs O(R * C) per query. Preparing something once could make each query cheap.
In one dimension, prefix[i] = sum of the first i elements lets you answer a range in O(1). Build the same idea for the rectangle from the top-left corner to each cell.

Let P[i][j] be the sum of the rectangle spanning rows 0..i-1 and columns 0..j-1. A query equals P[r2+1][c2+1] - P[r1][c2+1] - P[r2+1][c1] + P[r1][c1] (inclusion-exclusion: the corner was subtracted twice, so add it back once).
editorial: Build a table P of size (R + 1) x (C + 1) where P[i][j] is the sum of all cells in the top-left i x j rectangle. It fills in O(R * C) with the recurrence P[i][j] = matrix[i-1][j-1] + P[i-1][j] + P[i][j-1] - P[i-1][j-1]; the last term removes the overlap that both neighbours include.

Any rectangle is the big top-left rectangle ending at its bottom-right corner, minus the strip above it, minus the strip to its left, plus the corner rectangle that was subtracted twice. That is four table lookups, so every query is O(1).
Total time is O(R * C + q) and the extra space is O(R * C). The extra row and column of zeros in P avoid special cases for rectangles touching the border.
